episode_title: An AI state of the union: We've passed the inflection point, dark factories are coming, and automation timelines
summary: 1 hour 40 min. Simon Willison on why November 2025 was the inflection point for coding agents; his three agentic engineering patterns (red/green TDD, templates, hoarding); the 'dark factory' pattern where AI does its own QA without human review; writes 95% of code from his phone. YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wc8FBhQtdsA

episode_title: How Intercom 2x'd their engineering velocity in 9 months with Claude Code
summary: 1 hr 19 min. Hosted by Claire Vo. Intercom doubled merged PRs per R&D employee in 9 months. 100% of engineers plus non-engineers shipping code via Claude Code. 13 plugins, 100+ skills. Telemetry infrastructure for measuring AI adoption. Production-safe hooks (read-replica DB access, Okta auth, DynamoDB audit trail).

episode_title: Paper's vision for the future of design tooling
summary: Stephen Haney discusses how Paper fundamentally changes the speed of traditional design flows by putting code components onto a design canvas with real React and Tailwind, enabling designers to export production-ready components.

episode_title: The 2026 AI Design Field Report (tools, process, and what's working)
summary: Field report on how top design teams are using AI in 2026. Covers tools, process changes, and what's actually working vs hype.

episode_title: Steve Yegge's Vibe Coding Manifesto — Why Claude Code Is the Future
summary: Steve Yegge discusses why the 2024 tech stack is becoming obsolete, the importance of trusting agents, and orchestrating agents like a 'NASCAR pit crew' as a shift away from traditional IDE-based development.

episode_title: Brian Scanlan: Building AI-First at Intercom
summary: Deeper technical discussion of Intercom's AI-first engineering transformation, focusing on the Ruby on Rails backend context and how Claude Code integrates with production systems.

episode_title: Claude Code: Anthropic's CLI Agent
summary: Boris Cherny (creator of Claude Code) and Cat Wu (PM) on Claude Code's origins as an internal hack, its architecture, and roadmap. First deep technical interview about Claude Code.

episode_title: Head of Claude Code: What happens after coding is solved
summary: Boris Cherny on the post-coding future, Claude Code's growth to 4% of public GitHub commits, and what comes next when AI handles routine coding.

episode_title: The Creators of Model Context Protocol
summary: David Soria Parra and Justin Spahr-Summers on MCP's origins, design decisions, and protocol evolution. The canonical technical deep-dive on MCP.

episode_title: Extreme Harness Engineering: 1M LOC, 1B toks/day, 0% human code, 0% human review
summary: Ryan Lopopolo on building a 1M LOC codebase with zero human-written or reviewed code. Defines 'Harness Engineering' as the structured constraints that make this possible. Highly relevant to repo-template-governance.

episode_title: Advanced Claude Code techniques: context loading, mermaid diagrams, stop hooks, and more
summary: John Lindquist (Claude Code Ambassador at Vercel) demos advanced techniques: context loading via mermaid diagrams, stop hooks, automated code quality checks. Practical skills-focused episode.

episode_title: The internal AI tool that's transforming how Stripe designs products
summary: Owen Williams (design manager, Stripe) on Protodash — Stripe's internal AI prototyping platform. Shows how a design team built a full prototyping studio on top of Cursor rules + React components.

episode_title: What Comes After the IDE
summary: Amelia Wattenberger on Intent (her Augment Code product) and what developer workspaces look like when agents do most of the work. Directly addresses the unified-project-layer pain point.

episode_title: Shopify's AI Phase Transition
summary: Shopify CTO on critique loops > parallel agents — one agent critiques another rather than running many in parallel. Practical pattern for solo Claude Code users: trade latency for higher review-to-generation ratio.

episode_title: Notion's Token Town
summary: Notion rebuilt its agents 4-5 times. Key lesson: simplify the abstraction the model sees (XML → Markdown → SQL-like). Agents coordinate via native primitives (databases, pages, webhooks). Co-guest: Sarah Sachs.

episode_title: Marc Andreessen Introspects on The Death of the Browser
summary: Tier 2: industry commentary on browser → agent OS transition (Pi, OpenClaw). Useful framing context, not a workflow episode.

episode_title: Dreamer: the Personal Agent OS
summary: David Singleton (ex-Stripe CTO) launches Dreamer — natural-language agent authoring with full-stack infra. Adaptation gap: consumer product, but the 'Sidekick + agents' pattern informs solo-dev internal-tooling design.

episode_title: Why Anthropic Thinks AI Should Have Its Own Computer
summary: Anthropic's Claude Cowork desktop app: skills as portable automation, sandboxed delegation, native Chrome/DOM access over MCP-only flows, execute-test-iterate over heavy specs. Direct guidance for Claude Code subscribers.

episode_title: Retrieval After RAG: Hybrid Search, Agents, and Database Design
summary: Turbopuffer founder on agentic retrieval: parallel concurrent queries replacing single retrieval calls. Practical: when adding RAG/MCP to a Claude Code project, expect bursts of parallel reads — pick a backend that scales accordingly.

episode_title: NVIDIA's AI Engineers (Brev + Dynamo)
summary: Kyle Kranen (Dynamo) and Nader Khalil (Brev) on planetary-scale agent inference and CLI-first GPU access. Tier 2 infra context — explains downward pressure on Claude API/Code pricing.

episode_title: Cursor's Third Era: Cloud Agents
summary: Cursor's cloud agents auto-test before returning PRs; review by watching demo videos, not diffs. Slash commands /repro and /no_test, parallel best-of-N runs, 'grind mode' for multi-day agents. Adaptation gap: Cursor-specific UX, but the patterns translate to Claude Code multi-agent workflows.

episode_title: Every Agent Needs a Box
summary: Aaron Levie on the agent sandbox pattern: bounded filesystem access, distinct identity per agent, persistent workspace, continuous oversight (vs. human-employee privacy). Direct frame for solo-dev Claude Code subagent isolation.

episode_title: How to Kill the Code Review
summary: Aviator's Ankit Jain argues spec-driven verification replaces line-by-line review. Layered stack: multi-attempt agents + deterministic guardrails + BDD specs + permissions + adversarial verification. Direct guidance for Claude Code review hooks.

episode_title: Dylan Patel of SemiAnalysis on $200B AI CapEx
summary: Tier 2 industry context: hyperscaler $180-200B/year capex thesis. Affects Claude API/Code pricing and capacity over the next 18 months.

episode_title: METR's Joel Becker on exponential Time Horizon Evals
summary: METR researcher on Time Horizon Evals — measuring how long an agent stays on-task. The framing the field has converged on for evaluating long-running coding agents.

episode_title: Anthropic Distillation & How Models Cheat
summary: Nathan Lambert (Ai2) and Sebastian Raschka on distillation, reward hacking, and how models 'cheat' on benchmarks. SAIL Live #6. Tier 2 research context for Claude model selection.

episode_title: Claude Code for Finance + The Global Memory Shortage
summary: Claude Code's 1-year anniversary special. Doug O'Laughlin (SemiAnalysis) on using Claude Code as 'junior analyst' for financial research — a knowledge-work adaptation pattern. Plus the looming HBM/memory supply crunch.

episode_title: The End of SWE-Bench Verified
summary: OpenAI frontier evals team retires SWE-Bench Verified — 60%+ of remaining problems unsolvable due to narrow specs and training contamination. Endorses SWE-Bench Pro. Co-guest: Olivia Watkins.

episode_title: Bitter Lessons in Venture vs Growth
summary: Martin Casado and Sarah Wang (a16z) on capital, compute, and talent dynamics in AI. Tier 2 commentary for context, not a workflow episode.

episode_title: Owning the AI Pareto Frontier
summary: Jeff Dean on Google's TPU/model co-design and where the Pareto frontier between cost and capability sits. Tier 2 framing for Claude model selection (Haiku vs Sonnet vs Opus trade-offs).

episode_title: Captaining IMO Gold, Deep Think, On-Policy RL
summary: Yi Tay (Google DeepMind) on shipping Gemini Deep Think and IMO Gold. End-to-end RL approach over symbolic systems. Tier 3 research depth, useful context on reasoning-mode trade-offs.

episode_title: Brex's AI Hail Mary
summary: Brex CTO James Reggio on the AI-first transformation: open tool selection (Cursor + Windsurf + Claude Code via ConductorOne), custom multi-agent framework on TypeScript/Mastra, Greptile for AI code review, internal LLM gateway since Jan 2023, re-interviewed all engineers on agentic coding.

episode_title: Artificial Analysis: Independent LLM Evals as a Service
summary: George Cameron and Micah Hill-Smith on running independent LLM evals (hallucination, agentic tasks, openness). Useful when picking models — AA's numbers are the trusted third-party reference.

episode_title: LMArena's $1.7B Vision
summary: LMArena cofounder on the human-preference leaderboard's $150M Series A at $1.7B. Berkeley basement → de-facto industry standard. Tier 2 evals context.

summary: Tier 3 — pure research. Alex Lupsasca on GPT-5.x deriving new theoretical-physics/quantum-gravity results. Outside editorial lens but a high-signal example of frontier-model use.
